claims.text: CALPHAD can be used to assess phase stability in high-entropy alloys.
CALPHAD can be used to refine the microstructure of high-entropy alloys.
CALPHAD can be used to optimize the properties of high-entropy alloys.
Applying CALPHAD provides thermodynamic calculations and phase predictions.
CALPHAD can be applied across various temperatures, atmospheres, and processing conditions.
Gibbs free energy and phase diagrams are the relevant thermodynamic mediators for the proposed optimization.
CALPHAD provides a framework for understanding thermodynamic properties and phase stability in high-entropy alloys.
CALPHAD enables prediction of phase transitions in high-entropy alloys.
CALPHAD enables prediction of microstructure evolution in high-entropy alloys.
The properties of high-entropy alloys depend strongly on their phases, making phase prediction relevant to property optimization.
CALPHAD optimization will improve phase stability in high-entropy alloys relative to an unoptimized baseline.
CALPHAD optimization will produce a refined microstructure in high-entropy alloys relative to an unoptimized baseline.
CALPHAD optimization will produce optimized material properties in high-entropy alloys relative to an unoptimized baseline.
Reliable CALPHAD predictions require accurate thermodynamic data.
Kinetic effects can influence phase stability and limit equilibrium thermodynamic predictions.
The complexity of high-entropy alloy systems and experimental errors create uncertainty in CALPHAD prediction accuracy.
XRD, TEM, and DSC measurements can be used to compare predicted phase composition, microstructure, and thermodynamic behavior with experiments.
A significant deviation between experimental results and CALPHAD predictions would falsify the hypothesis.
